_comment: Octail's own egg (plan §6.4), built on games-steamcmd windrose/egg-windrose.json (pelican-eggs, MIT licence) and checked against the app's Steam data (app 4129620: the Windows depot, WindroseServer.exe -log). The Windows server runs under Proton (Xalia off as upstream) and its log (R5/Saved/Logs/R5.log) is followed on the console. R5/ServerDescription.json is made by the install once, with a random invite code (upstream: the shared default "server1"), and the Startup tab's name, password, player limit, region and connection mode are set in it before every start (json parser); the direct connection port is always the server's main port, the password switch follows the password (set at start), and the invite code is only replaced when the Startup tab has one. Upstream's world name and difficulty variables are left out (they set nothing). The server ignores Ctrl+C under Proton (a smoke run on vm1 was killed after 120 s): the stop trap gives it 30 s, then SIGTERM; it writes its world records every 60 s. Install sandbox defaults and resource hints, the anonymous login only, and the install fails when SteamCMD didn't download the server. SteamCMD is retried up to 3 times: its first run on a fresh install often fails with "Missing configuration". SteamCMD exits 0 even when an install failed (Missing configuration), so its retry loop counts a run as done only on SteamCMD's "Success! App" line.
name: Windrose
author: eggs@octail.net
description: Survive as a pirate in the Age of Sail: build a ship and a base, explore islands and fight at sea with your crew. The Windows dedicated server, run under Proton.

startup_commands.Default: export PROTON_DISABLE_XALIA=1; if [ -n "${SERVER_PASSWORD}" ]; then WR_PROTECTED=true; else WR_PROTECTED=false; fi; sed -i -E "s/(\"IsPasswordProtected\": *)(true|false)/\1${WR_PROTECTED}/" R5/ServerDescription.json; [ -z "${INVITE_CODE}" ] || sed -i -E "s/(\"InviteCode\": *\")[^\"]*\"/\1${INVITE_CODE}\"/" R5/ServerDescription.json; grep -o '"InviteCode": *"[^"]*"' R5/ServerDescription.json; proton run ./R5/Binaries/Win64/WindroseServer-Win64-Shipping.exe -log & WR_PID=$!; trap "for i in $(seq 1 30); do kill -0 ${WR_PID} 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 1; done; pkill -TERM -f WindroseServer-Win64-Shipping 2>/dev/null; wait ${WR_PID}" INT TERM; tail -c0 -F ./R5/Saved/Logs/R5.log --pid=${WR_PID} 2>/dev/null & wait ${WR_PID}

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
## Octail curated install: SteamCMD downloads the Windows build of the server (it runs under Proton).
## Server Files: /mnt/server

## anonymous login: this server needs no Steam account
STEAM_USER=anonymous
STEAM_PASS=""
STEAM_AUTH=""

## download and install steamcmd (the small archive goes to /tmp, the game straight to the server's disk)
cd /tmp || exit 1
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamcmd
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 300 --retry 3 --retry-delay 5 -o steamcmd.tar.gz https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/client/installer/steamcmd_linux.tar.gz || { echo "Downloading SteamCMD failed."; exit 1; }
tar -xzvf steamcmd.tar.gz -C /mnt/server/steamcmd
rm -f steamcmd.tar.gz
mkdir -p /mnt/server/steamapps # Fix steamcmd disk write error when this folder is missing
cd /mnt/server/steamcmd || exit 1

# SteamCMD fails otherwise for some reason, even running as root.
# This is changed at the end of the install process anyways.
chown -R root:root /mnt
export HOME=/mnt/server

## install game using steamcmd
## Octail: SteamCMD's first run often fails with "Missing configuration"; try up to 3 times
for steamcmd_try in 1 2 3; do
    if ./steamcmd.sh +force_install_dir /mnt/server +login ${STEAM_USER} ${STEAM_PASS} ${STEAM_AUTH} $( [[ "${WINDOWS_INSTALL}" == "1" ]] && printf %s '+@sSteamCmdForcePlatformType windows' ) +app_update ${SRCDS_APPID} $( [[ -z ${SRCDS_BETAID} ]] || printf %s "-beta ${SRCDS_BETAID}" ) $( [[ -z ${SRCDS_BETAPASS} ]] || printf %s "-betapassword ${SRCDS_BETAPASS}" ) validate +quit 2>&1 | tee /tmp/steamcmd.log && grep -q "Success! App '" /tmp/steamcmd.log && ! grep -q "ERROR! Failed to install app" /tmp/steamcmd.log; then break; fi
    echo "SteamCMD did not finish (attempt $steamcmd_try of 3)"
done

## set up 32 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk32
cp -v linux32/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk32/steamclient.so

## set up 64 bit libraries
mkdir -p /mnt/server/.steam/sdk64
cp -v linux64/steamclient.so ../.steam/sdk64/steamclient.so

## Octail: fail the install when SteamCMD didn't download the server
if [[ ! -f "/mnt/server/R5/Binaries/Win64/WindroseServer-Win64-Shipping.exe" ]]; then
    echo -e "\nSteamCMD failed to install the Windrose dedicated server; try reinstalling."
    exit 1
fi

## Octail: R5/ServerDescription.json is made once (the server makes it on its first start, but the panel sets the
## Startup tab's values in it before every start, json parser), with a random invite code; an existing file is kept.
mkdir -p /mnt/server/R5
if [[ ! -f /mnt/server/R5/ServerDescription.json ]]; then
    INVITE="oct$(tr -dc 'a-z0-9' < /dev/urandom | head -c 9)"
    cat > /mnt/server/R5/ServerDescription.json <<EOF
{
  "Version": 1,
  "DeploymentId": "",
  "ServerDescription_Persistent": {
    "PersistentServerId": "",
    "InviteCode": "${INVITE}",
    "IsPasswordProtected": false,
    "Password": "",
    "ServerName": "Octail Windrose Server",
    "WorldIslandId": "",
    "MaxPlayerCount": 4,
    "UserSelectedRegion": "",
    "P2pProxyAddress": "0.0.0.0",
    "UseDirectConnection": false,
    "DirectConnectionServerAddress": "",
    "DirectConnectionServerPort": 7777,
    "DirectConnectionProxyAddress": "0.0.0.0",
    "AutoLoadLatestBackupIfHasBroken": true
  }
}
EOF
    echo "Invite code: ${INVITE}"
fi

## install end
echo "-----------------------------------------"
echo "Installation completed..."
echo "-----------------------------------------"

variables.name: Server Name
variables.description: The name players see (must contain a letter; no double quotes or backslashes).

variables.name: Invite Code
variables.description: Optional: the code players join with (6 to 32 letters and digits, with at least one letter; case-sensitive). Empty = keep the one the install made (shown on the console at every start).

variables.name: Server Password
variables.description: Optional: players must enter it to join. Empty = no password (no spaces; must contain a letter).

variables.name: Max Players
variables.description: Up to 4 runs best; up to 10 works with enough memory (16 GB).

variables.name: Region
variables.description: The relay and matchmaking region: SEA, CIS or EU (EU also covers North America). Empty = picked by latency.

variables.name: Direct Connection
variables.description: false: players connect through the invite code (no open port needed). true: they connect straight to the main port (TCP and UDP), which must be reachable.

variables.name: Auto Update
variables.description: Update the server with SteamCMD before every start (1 = on, 0 = off).

variables.name: Windows Install
variables.description: Downloads the Windows build (the server runs under Proton).
